review_notes: I read the whole file and the simp lemmas it depends on in ProcyclicPowerIndex.lean and ProcyclicPowerLimit.lean. I did not run Lean, so the findings come from reading the rule shapes (subterm-first rewriting, overlapping left-hand sides) and are not simp traces. I did not flag the type-level `_obj` simp lemmas or the `map_id`/`map_apply` overlap. They look benign or too speculative to support. I did not confirm whether Mathlib's `Iso.inv_hom_id_apply` is simp. Finding 2 therefore says the lemma may be redundant.

findings.problem: The simp normal form for a residue coordinate stops at `(NatIso).inv.app n (mk' _ x)`. The file has simp lemmas for the component (`residuePowerQuotientComponent_inv_apply`) and for `residuePowerQuotientNatIso_hom_apply`. It has no simp lemma that unfolds `.inv.app n` of `residuePowerQuotientNatIso` or of `…OfInfiniteSupport`. Both are irreducible defs, so simp cannot see through them. `_apply` and `_generator` also both match `(… g).val n`. `_apply` has the more general left-hand side. If it fires first, the coordinate of the generator is stuck at `inv.app n (mk' g)`. The `_generator` proof has to bypass simp with `change` and `congrArg ULift.up` for this reason.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] residuePowerQuotientNatIso_inv_apply` with the same shape as the existing `_hom_apply`, with right-hand side `ULift.up ((powerImage_zmodContinuousMulEquiv … (hindex n)).symm q)`. Add a matching lemma for `…OfInfiniteSupport`, or make that def `abbrev`/reducible. Then `_apply` rewrites to `ULift.up (equiv.symm (mk' x))`. The existing simp lemma `powerImage_zmodContinuousMulEquiv_symm_apply_generator` closes the generator case, so `_generator` no longer competes with `_apply` and follows by `simp`.
findings.benefit: One canonical coordinate normal form (`ULift.up (equiv.symm …)`) replaces the stuck `inv.app`. The generator coordinate then simplifies to `ULift.up (ofAdd 1)` whichever lemma fires first.

findings.problem: The left-hand side `….hom.app n (( … x).val n)` contains the left-hand side of the simp lemma `continuousMulEquivSupportedResidueLimit_apply` as a proper subterm. Simp rewrites inner subterms first, so `_apply` turns the argument into `….inv.app n (mk' _ x)` before this lemma is tried. This lemma is then unlikely ever to fire. The simp set effectively proves it by `_apply` followed by `Iso.inv_hom_id_apply`, which is exactly the lemma's own proof, so it adds nothing to the simp set. It is either dead as a simp lemma or redundant.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` from `continuousMulEquivSupportedResidueLimit_quotient_apply` and keep it as a plain lemma for `rw`. Alternatively, delete it if `simp` closes the goal using `_apply` plus the categorical `inv_hom_id` simp lemma.
findings.benefit: The simp set contains only rules that can fire. It no longer has an unreachable rule that overlaps `_apply`, and the normal form for residue coordinates stays unambiguous.

Its proof is `rw [hom_apply, powerImage_zmodContinuousMulEquiv_apply_one]`, and the second lemma is already `@[simp]`. Both lemmas match `hom (up (ofAdd 1))`. findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `residuePowerQuotientComponent_hom_one`, and keep it as a named convenience lemma or delete it.
findings.benefit: A smaller, non-overlapping simp set that is easier to reason about. No simp behaviour is lost, because `hom_apply` followed by `apply_one` gives the same result.
